To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we generated a mouse lacking Mrp2 (ABCC 2) and studied the role of Mrpr2 in vivo, in particular with regard to its function in drug transport and in protection against food-derived carcinogens.
we have developed an animal model to study the pharmacological and toxicological functions of the multidrug resistance protein 2 (Mrp2).

we have generated a Mrp2- (Abcc2-) knockout mouse, which was viable and fertile but had an increased plasma concentration of food-derived carcinogens after oral administration and of the anticancer drug methotrexate at a high dose after i.v. injection, and a Mrp2/Mdr1a/b (Abcc2/Mdr1ab-) knockout mouse, whose biliary excretion after i.v. doxorubicin administration was decreased 54-fold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of knockout mice for the ATP binding cassette (ABC) transporter Mrp2 (also called MRP2 or cMOAT).
the transport of drugs and other xenotoxines by the multidrug resistance protein 2 (MRP2), which is a member of the ATP-binding-cassett (ABC) transporter family.
multidrug resistance (MDR), which is the phenomenon of cancer cells to become resistant to a broad range of chemotherapeutic drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mrp1-/-/2-/-/3-/-/4-/-/6-/- mouse would be a valuable tool to study the role of the Mrp transporters in drug and xenobiotic disposition.
the MRP2 (MRP3) knockout mice are useful for the study of the role of MRP2 (and MRP3) in the transport of endo- and xenobiotics.
Mrp2 is the most important efflux transporter for xenobiotics and endobiotics in liver and kidney, and it is the main determinant of the biliary excretion process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mrp2 is an important barrier against exposure to food-derived carcinogens and that the Mrp1-Mrp2-Mrp3-Mrp4 axis is a crucial efflux system in the liver and kidney.
the Mdr1/Mrp2 double knockout mouse is a valuable tool for the study of the combined effect of Mdr1a and Mrp2 on the disposition and toxicity of anticancer drugs.
Mdr1a/Mdr1b/Mrp1/Mrp2/Mrp3/Mrp4/Mrp5 knockout mouse strains are available for studies of drug and xenotoxin transport and disposition in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mrp2 is an essential transporter for the excretion of bilirubi, bile acids, glutathione, and glutathione conjugates.
the Mrp knockout mice are a very important tool to study the impact of Mrps on behavior of drugs.
Mrp2 knockout animals can be used to study the pharmacology and physiology of Mrp2.
